preamble: Loss of glottalization in the glottalized palatal approximant (Americanist y̓). In Makah the Proto-Southern-Wakashan glottalized sonorants merged with the plain ones, with compensatory lengthening of the preceding vowel (Davidson 2002: 76, citing Jacobsen 1968), so Nuu-chah-nulth y̓ corresponds to Makah y. Upriver Halkomelem lost resonant glottalization, usually lengthening the preceding vowel, while Island and Downriver keep it (Compton & Gerdts 2005): Downriver sqʷəmey̓, Upriver sqwemá:y 'dog'. In Quileute, Proto-Chimakuan *y̓ became y or ʔy (Powell 1974, as summarized on Wikipedia); the words below show the glottal stop before the plain glide. Chemakum instead hardened *y̓ to (ʔ)č.

languageExamples.context: Davidson (2002: 76): the Proto-Southern-Wakashan glottalized sonorants merged with the plain sonorants in Makah, with compensatory lengthening of the preceding vowel (citing Jacobsen 1968); Nuu-chah-nulth keeps them

examples.from: PSW *y̓, as kept in Nuu-chah-nulth ʔ̴uy̓i 'medicine'
examples.note: Davidson (2002: 76), ex. (127). The long u· before y is the compensatory lengthening. Davidson writes the Nuu-chah-nulth pharyngealized glottal stop as ʔ̴. The initial consonants differ because PSW *q̓ is kept in Makah but became ʔ̴ in Nuu-chah-nulth (Davidson 2002: 75, ex. (126), after Jacobsen 1969a).

examples.note: Wiktionary (sqwemá:y). The headword carries no dialect label, but the page cites Galloway's Dictionary of Upriver Halkomelem (2009), and Wikipedia gives hən̓q̓əmin̓əm̓ as the name of the Downriver dialect. The page also lists the cognates Squamish sḵwemáy̓ and Klallam sqʷəmə́y̕.
